before.rope_note: Blewett Pass Table Mountain trail through a burn area to Tronsen Head/larch meadows; this is effectively a hiking trail, consistent with the Class 2 rating. No technical gear needed.

itinerary.cal: Artist Point road (WA-542) typically doesn't open until snow clears, often not until July; the route is usually snow-covered well into early summer.

days.note: A short, popular half-day outing above treeline. From the Artist Point trailhead (~5,100 ft), switchback up a short cliff band onto the broad Table Mountain plateau, then walk the open tableland east with big views of Mt. Baker, Ptarmigan Ridge, and the Chain Lakes basin to a pair of tarns mirroring Mt. Shuksan - the standard turnaround. Strong parties can continue on unmarked, looser scramble terrain toward the high point or down toward Chain Lakes, but most hikers simply retrace their steps.
days.title: Artist Point to Table Mountain plateau (car-to-car)

schedule.label: Leave Artist Point trailhead
schedule.detail: Parking area at ~5,100 ft; a Northwest Forest Pass is required.

schedule.label: Top of switchbacks
schedule.detail: Gain ~400 ft up the cliff band; views open over Heather Meadows.

schedule.label: Reach the plateau rim
schedule.detail: Mt. Baker, Ptarmigan Ridge, and Chain Lakes basin come into view.

schedule.label: Twin tarns / standard turnaround
schedule.detail: Mt. Shuksan reflections; most parties turn back here (2.6 mi RT).

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Reverse the trail; total outing under 2.5 hrs for most hikers.

days.objective: Reach the twin tarns viewpoint below Mt. Shuksan; optional scramble to the true summit

itinerary.totalNote: A short, popular half-day scramble: roughly 1.5-2.5 hrs car-to-car for the standard 2.6 mi round trip to the tarns, ~725 ft gain - not an overnight trip.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late July through September; early July and October are workable but marginal due to lingering snow or early-season road/weather risk

July.reason: Artist Point road often only opens mid-July; the cliff-notch switchbacks can still hold steep, consolidated snow into early-mid July, so early July is marginal without an axe/microspikes

August.reason: Trail typically fully melted out, driest and busiest month, best all-around conditions

October.reason: First snows and shortening daylight/weather windows can return; still climbable in a dry stretch but less reliable

September.reason: Still dry and stable, thinner crowds than August

before.beta: From the Artist Point parking lot (about 5,075 ft), the Table Mountain Trail climbs a series of tight, exposed switchbacks cut into the mountain's southeast-facing rock face for roughly 0.6-1 mile to gain the broad summit plateau near 5,700 ft. Beyond the switchbacks the trail is gentle, crossing the plateau to tarns with Shuksan views around the 1.3-mile mark; most hikers turn around there. The trail continues west and eventually drops to link with the Chain Lakes Trail system. The route is entirely above treeline, narrow and cliff-edge in its lower half, and not recommended for those uneasy with exposure, small children, or dogs.
watch_out: Switchbacks are steep, exposed, and not recommended for anyone uneasy with heights, small children, or dogs
North side beyond the tarns drops steeply (700-800 ft) to the Chain Lakes Trail via an unmarked, sketchy scramble — stay on the established trail unless experienced at off-trail route-finding
Small Artist Point lot (~160 cars) fills early on summer weekends
Avoid kicking rocks loose on the switchbacks — other hikers are often below

emergency.notes: Cell service is unreliable to nonexistent at Artist Point and on the mountain; plan accordingly.
emergency.rangerStation: Glacier Public Service Center, 10091 Mt. Baker Hwy, Glacier, WA 98244
emergency.nearestHospital: PeaceHealth St. Joseph Medical Center, Bellingham (~53 miles / ~1 hr drive from Artist Point)
emergency.sheriffDispatch: Whatcom County Sheriff's Office (911) dispatches Whatcom County Search & Rescue
